title: Wheel of Fortune Meaning: Adjust as Circumstances Change

quickTake.upright: Things are moving. Opportunities and uncertainties are arriving together, so adjust as you go.
quickTake.reversed: Change is not following your timetable. Steady yourself, then see which step you can adjust.

hook: Some changes move faster than your plans. The Wheel of Fortune draws attention to timing, cycles and the response you can still choose.

sections.title: Follow the wheel, then look at the four corners
sections.bodyMarkdown:
A large orange wheel fills the centre of a blue sky and clouds. Several concentric rings divide its surface, with spokes radiating from the middle. Latin and Hebrew letters appear on the outer ring, and further symbols inside. A blue sphinx sits on top, holding a sword in its forelimbs. A yellow serpent descends on the left. At the lower right, a red figure with a human body and a long-snouted animal head curves upward along the rim, supporting it.

Each corner contains a winged figure with a book: a human figure at upper left, an eagle at upper right, a bull at lower left and a lion at lower right. The curved rim and flanking bodies suggest motion, while the four corners hold the composition steady. No one turns a handle, and no ordinary person controls the whole scene. [View the card](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:RWS_Tarot_10_Wheel_of_Fortune.jpg)

sections.title: Mixed symbolism does not prove an Egyptian origin
sections.bodyMarkdown: Waite says he adopted and adapted Éliphas Lévi’s design. He connects the corner figures with the four living creatures of Ezekiel, the wheel with the flux of human life, and the sphinx with balance within it. He explicitly says that using Egyptian symbolism does not establish an Egyptian origin for tarot. The mixture belongs to this particular symbolic arrangement. [Waite, Part II, X](https://original.sacred-texts.com/tarot/pkt/pktar10.htm)

sections.title: Upright: Notice openings and leave some room
sections.bodyMarkdown:
Our upright reading focuses on changing conditions. A previously closed route may open, while a familiar method may need updating. You can take an opportunity while checking how long it lasts, its conditions and its actual costs. Responding to the moment means using new information, not treating every coincidence as an instruction.

The wheel keeps turning, and progress still needs care. When a collaboration first attracts attention, organising capacity and routines is more practical than assuming the interest will last indefinitely.

sections.title: Reversed: Separate setbacks, excess and repetition
sections.bodyMarkdown:
Modern readings often use the reversed card to explore feeling stuck, repeating patterns or resisting change. We use that approach to practise adaptability, but it is not Waite’s wording. His reversed entry lists increase, abundance and superfluity. Another useful question is therefore whether opportunities are arriving faster than your resources can handle. [Waite, Part III, §3, entry 10](https://original.sacred-texts.com/tarot/pkt/pkt0303.htm)

Identify what has actually changed. Has an external condition delayed the schedule, or do you keep returning to the same approach despite feedback? The first may call for a buffer and an alternative plan; the second may require a different method. They are not the same kind of “bad luck.”

sections.title: When events outrun the plan
sections.bodyMarkdown:
If a flight changes, first confirm the new time, then reorganise transfers and accommodation. List what can be changed or refunded and when decisions are needed. Here the card helps organise your response; it cannot reveal the airline’s next decision.

A small shop suddenly receives many orders. Upright, the card can prompt you to use the opening in demand; reversed, to check whether you are overcommitted. Give realistic delivery dates, limit additional orders if necessary, then consider extra help.

If several applications for the same kind of role go nowhere, compare your materials and the feedback. Distinguish hiring conditions in the industry from problems in your résumé. Drawing a “lucky” card is no reason to skip preparation, place bets or seek investment returns.

sections.title: Practice: Leave a way to adapt
sections.bodyMarkdown: Make three columns: conditions that have changed; actions I can adjust; things I cannot currently control. Choose one small action from the second column for today, and write an alternative plan. A few days later, review what actually happened instead of looking only for coincidences that fit the card.

sections.bodyMarkdown: The Wheel does not guarantee approaching good luck or decree that bad events must repeat. Its most useful question is: now that circumstances have changed, am I still following an outdated plan?

articleMarkdown:
# Wheel of Fortune Meaning: Adjust as Circumstances Change

Card: Wheel of Fortune  
Number: X · RWS Major Arcana  
Keywords: Turning points, Cycles, Adaptability

**Upright quick take:** Things are moving. Opportunities and uncertainties are arriving together, so adjust as you go.  
**Reversed quick take:** Change is not following your timetable. Steady yourself, then see which step you can adjust.

Some changes move faster than your plans. The Wheel of Fortune draws attention to timing, cycles and the response you can still choose.

## Follow the wheel, then look at the four corners

A large orange wheel fills the centre of a blue sky and clouds. Several concentric rings divide its surface, with spokes radiating from the middle. Latin and Hebrew letters appear on the outer ring, and further symbols inside. A blue sphinx sits on top, holding a sword in its forelimbs. A yellow serpent descends on the left. At the lower right, a red figure with a human body and a long-snouted animal head curves upward along the rim, supporting it.

Each corner contains a winged figure with a book: a human figure at upper left, an eagle at upper right, a bull at lower left and a lion at lower right. The curved rim and flanking bodies suggest motion, while the four corners hold the composition steady. No one turns a handle, and no ordinary person controls the whole scene. [View the card](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:RWS_Tarot_10_Wheel_of_Fortune.jpg)

## Mixed symbolism does not prove an Egyptian origin

Waite says he adopted and adapted Éliphas Lévi’s design. He connects the corner figures with the four living creatures of Ezekiel, the wheel with the flux of human life, and the sphinx with balance within it. He explicitly says that using Egyptian symbolism does not establish an Egyptian origin for tarot. The mixture belongs to this particular symbolic arrangement. [Waite, Part II, X](https://original.sacred-texts.com/tarot/pkt/pktar10.htm)

## Upright: Notice openings and leave some room

Our upright reading focuses on changing conditions. A previously closed route may open, while a familiar method may need updating. You can take an opportunity while checking how long it lasts, its conditions and its actual costs. Responding to the moment means using new information, not treating every coincidence as an instruction.

The wheel keeps turning, and progress still needs care. When a collaboration first attracts attention, organising capacity and routines is more practical than assuming the interest will last indefinitely.

## Reversed: Separate setbacks, excess and repetition

Modern readings often use the reversed card to explore feeling stuck, repeating patterns or resisting change. We use that approach to practise adaptability, but it is not Waite’s wording. His reversed entry lists increase, abundance and superfluity. Another useful question is therefore whether opportunities are arriving faster than your resources can handle. [Waite, Part III, §3, entry 10](https://original.sacred-texts.com/tarot/pkt/pkt0303.htm)

Identify what has actually changed. Has an external condition delayed the schedule, or do you keep returning to the same approach despite feedback? The first may call for a buffer and an alternative plan; the second may require a different method. They are not the same kind of “bad luck.”

## When events outrun the plan

If a flight changes, first confirm the new time, then reorganise transfers and accommodation. List what can be changed or refunded and when decisions are needed. Here the card helps organise your response; it cannot reveal the airline’s next decision.

A small shop suddenly receives many orders. Upright, the card can prompt you to use the opening in demand; reversed, to check whether you are overcommitted. Give realistic delivery dates, limit additional orders if necessary, then consider extra help.

If several applications for the same kind of role go nowhere, compare your materials and the feedback. Distinguish hiring conditions in the industry from problems in your résumé. Drawing a “lucky” card is no reason to skip preparation, place bets or seek investment returns.

## Practice: Leave a way to adapt

Make three columns: conditions that have changed; actions I can adjust; things I cannot currently control. Choose one small action from the second column for today, and write an alternative plan. A few days later, review what actually happened instead of looking only for coincidences that fit the card.

## A common misreading

The Wheel does not guarantee approaching good luck or decree that bad events must repeat. Its most useful question is: now that circumstances have changed, am I still following an outdated plan?

## Read next

The Tower: compare cyclical movement with a sudden structural change; The World: compare changes within a cycle with the completion of a stage.

sourceRecord.hook: 有些变化来得比计划快。命运之轮把你的注意力带到时机、循环，以及此刻还能选择的回应。
sourceRecord.uprightQuickTake: 局面开始转动，机会和变数都来了，及时调整更有用。
sourceRecord.reversedQuickTake: 变化不按你的节奏来，先稳住，再看哪一步能改。

sections.title: 绕着轮看一圈，再看四个角
paragraphs: 蓝色天空与云团中，一只橙色大轮占据中央。轮面分成数层圆环，轮辐从中心向外伸出；外圈写有拉丁字母与希伯来字母，内圈另有符号。轮顶坐着蓝色斯芬克斯，前肢握剑。左边黄色蛇形身体朝下延伸，右下方红色、长吻的人身兽首形象沿着轮缘向上托起。
四角各有一只带翼的形象：左上是人形，右上是鹰，左下是牛，右下是狮子，身前都有书。中央轮缘的弧线和两侧身形让人想到运动，四角却把构图稳稳框住。画面里没有谁在扳动把手，也没有某个普通人独自控制全局。[查看本篇牌面](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:RWS_Tarot_10_Wheel_of_Fortune.jpg)

sections.title: 混合的象征，不等于埃及起源证明
paragraphs: Waite 说自己沿用并调整了 Éliphas Lévi 的构想，把四角形象联系到《以西结书》的四活物，把轮与人生流变相连，并让斯芬克斯代表其中的平衡。他也明确说，采用埃及象征不意味着主张塔罗起源于埃及。牌上的混合图像属于这套具体的象征安排。[Waite 第二部 X](https://original.sacred-texts.com/tarot/pkt/pktar10.htm)

sections.title: 正位 留意窗口，也留一点余量
paragraphs: 本站将正位读作条件正在改变：原先不通的路可能出现入口，熟悉的办法也可能需要更新。你可以抓住机会，同时检查它的有效期限、参与条件和实际成本。所谓顺势，是根据新信息行动，不是把所有偶然都解释成命令。
轮会转，已有进展仍要维护。一个合作刚获得关注时，及时整理流程与容量，比假设这股热度永远持续更实际。

sections.title: 逆位 不顺、过量和反复，都值得分开看
paragraphs: 现代读牌常把逆位用于思考卡住、反复或抗拒变化。本篇沿此方向练习应变，但不把它冒充 Waite 原句：他的逆位词条反而列了增加、丰盛与过量。于是另一个值得保留的问题是，机会是否来得太多，以至于你的资源接不住。[Waite 第三部 §3，第10条](https://original.sacred-texts.com/tarot/pkt/pkt0303.htm)
先看现实变化发生在哪儿。是排期被外部条件推迟，还是每次遇到反馈都重复旧做法？前者需要缓冲和备选安排，后者可能需要改方法。两者并不是同一种「运气差」。

sections.title: 计划赶不上变化时怎样用
paragraphs: 旅行遇到航班调整，先确认新时间，再重排接驳与住宿；把可退改项目和必须决定的节点列出来。牌在这里帮助你组织反应，无法判断航空公司的下一次安排。
小店突然收到大量订单，正位可提醒你利用需求窗口，逆位则提醒你检查是否接单过量。可以先给出真实交期、限制新增数量，再决定是否增加人手。
求职时，同一岗位几次没有进展。比较各次材料和反馈，区分行业招人节奏与简历呈现问题；不要因为抽到「幸运」就跳过准备，更不要据此下注或追求投资回报。

sections.title: 练习 给变化留一个出口
paragraphs: 画三栏：已经改变的条件、我能调整的动作、暂时无法控制的部分。只从第二栏选一件今天能做的小事，并写一个备选方案。过几天用实际发生的事回看，而不是只寻找与牌意相符的巧合。

sections.title: 容易看错的地方
paragraphs: 命运之轮不保证好运将至，也不宣判坏事必然循环。它最有用的提问是：局面变了以后，我是不是还在沿用过期的计划？
